title: Retire legacy OpenSSL shims and strengthen JWT/OAuth/SAML validation paths
creator: Olivia Park
description: Replace a set of outdated OpenSSL compatibility shims embedded across auth services, consolidate token validation logic into a single vetted library, and remediate SAML/OAuth edge cases discovered during the OpenSSL upgrade. Goal is to remove custom crypto adapters that complicate upgrades and auditing, reduce binary surface area, and ensure consistent cryptographic and token validation behavior across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: All services previously using legacy OpenSSL shims compile and pass CI with OpenSSL 3.1 runtime or BoringSSL-compatible API layer
Token validation is centralized in the new auth-token package with deterministic behavior and a single schema for token claims parsing
SAML Assertion consumer flows validated against test-suite including signed assertion edge cases (clock skew, audience mismatch, nested attributes)
No user-facing auth regressions in staging for 72 hours after canary rollout; automated smoke tests pass against staging and preprod
Security review sign-off and CVE scanning shows no remaining critical vulnerabilities in the new dependency surface
comments: 2025-02-18 - Olivia Park: Initial discovery: multiple services ship small OpenSSL shim layers to abstract 1.x vs 3.x APIs. These shims cause build divergence and block upgrades. Created spike to enumerate all repositories referencing crypto/shim folders.

2025-02-21 - Dmitri Ivanov: Spike results: 9 services directly import crypto/shim; 4 internal libs copy shim code. Prioritized by customer-facing auth path (token validation) and Dedicated control plane services.

2025-02-24 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/5823 - PoC replacing shim with unified adapter that targets OpenSSL 3.1 and optionally BoringSSL API. Includes feature-flag to toggle legacy behavior.

2025-02-27 - Code review notes from security: ensure RSA key parsing rejects leading zero-padding, normalize JWK kid handling, and add explicit algorithm allowlist. Updated PoC to include algorithm allowlist and stricter KID lookup.

2025-03-01 - Integration testing: added SAML assertion fixtures (expired, wrong-audience, nested-attributes) and observed previous shim accepted an invalid nested attribute case. Implemented assertion validation guard and added test coverage.
2025-03-03 - Release engineering: coordinated new build images with OpenSSL 3.1; container image tags: ghcr.io/redwood-inference/runtime:openssl-3.1-20250303. Draft rollout plan created.
2025-03-04 - PM review (Ayesha Reddy): Approved prioritization for this cycle. Requested explicit canary window and telemetry dashboards for token validation errors and SAML rejects.
Follow-ups: schedule security review session, add migration guide for Dedicated and Private customers, and list any third-party integrations that need public key redistribution notes.
testing_notes: Unit tests added for jwt claim canonicalization and algorithm allowlist
End-to-end staging harness includes: OAuth token exchange, refresh flows, SSO SAML login with Okta test tenant
Chaos test: restart auth services during token cache refresh to validate KV cache resilience
Performance: microbenchmarks show centralized token validation adds ~0.5ms median per auth request; acceptable under P50 SLOs with current batching
risk: Medium: changes touch core auth paths and crypto stack. Main risks are a subtle parsing regression allowing malformed tokens, or incompatibility with customer-managed SAML IdPs that rely on lenient parsing. Also risk of transient increased CPU from stricter validation logic during rollout.
rollback_plan: Feature-flagged rollout with the ability to toggle legacy adapter for up to 48 hours. If a critical regression is detected (auth failure rate >1% sustained for 10 minutes or key customer impact), revert flag and rollback to previous runtime image. Post-rollback: capture traces and failing tokens for forensic analysis.
